head: 06a096ca81095965250d0c07c113f869c80f2926
classification_reasons: Spec is tight: the intent's three open questions are answered, the one flagged concern (version) is decided, and acceptance is measurable.

Blast radius is not small in kind: every download goes through the hand-built HTTP opener, and pyproject.toml gains a Windows-only runtime dependency and a [tool.setuptools] packaging table, followed by guardrail edits the owner must sequence after merge.

Coverage: 20 new parametrized cases cover the code changes, and the existing with_retries, Vision and REST tests cover the error paths. No automated test covers the packaging half (R9-R11, tzdata on Windows); the owner's Windows check at deploy covers it.
attempted: Intent: all three outcomes are met by the diff. A 3xx is returned as its status and only https is opened (app/data/http.py opener). A naive or aware datetime bound raises InvalidRequestError, never TypeError (params.parse_date, checked before the date branch, since a datetime is a date). tzdata is declared for win32 only, and the packages are named so pip install -e . can build. ci.yml and the guardrail files are untouched. plan.md names the stale CLAUDE.md and sdlc.yaml lines for the owner, with the merge-order caveat.

Spec and plan: checked R1-R13 against the diff. The source and test diff touches exactly the files plan.md lists (tests/test_data.py, app/data/http.py, app/data/params.py, pyproject.toml, .gitignore, plan.md). The handler list, the comment and the error message match plan steps 2-4. Since the build gate, this phase changed only evidence and status.yaml: no code, test or packaging file.

Proof: failing-test.log is literal pytest output from the pre-fix tree. It shows 20 failed, matching the 20 new cases, with the expected failure modes: the redirect followed 4 more times, Connection refused or the file read for the scheme cases, and TypeError for the datetime cases. gate-build.json (the runner's run on fa325a5, the same code tree as HEAD) shows compileall exit 0, 89 passed and ruff clean. That is 69 pre-existing tests plus the 20 new ones, consistent with the intent's 69 on main. The test-phase verifier.md exercised the changed behaviour directly: each redirect status (only the origin opened), neighbouring statuses (200/404/418/429/500 unchanged), the Vision refusal path with one fetch and no retry, the http/ftp/file/data/HTTP/gopher schemes refused even with http_proxy/ftp_proxy set, the handler list, the datetime refusals via make_request, load_klines (before any fetch) and clear_cache, the unchanged date/str paths, and the wheel METADATA marker. test.log, build.log and lint.log carry the deferred-to-the-runner mark and the verifier says 'read, not run'. That is not missing proof; I left those logs to the runner.

Blast radius: callers of urllib_fetch (the loader's default fetch, the CLI) and of parse_date (make_request at params.py:104-105, cache.clear_cache at cache.py:146-147; no other caller in app/) still hold. Traced the hand-built opener. Non-2xx answers go HTTPErrorProcessor -> HTTPDefaultErrorHandler -> HTTPError -> the HttpResponse conversion in urllib_fetch, as before, so 4xx/5xx/418/429 are unchanged and a 3xx now takes the same path (status < 500, not retried). ProxyHandler.proxy_open returns None for an https request (tunnel), so _HTTPSHandler and its timeouts still serve proxied requests. An http/ftp request with an env proxy re-enters open() as http and hits UnknownHandler. TLS context untouched. No risk-list item, no schema, cache layout or public API change, no guardrail file in the diff.

Policies: security-baseline (a bounded transport, no live network in the tests, the new dependency carries its Risks line). coding-standards (type hints on the new tests, the fix-type change ships tests first, the dependency is Windows-only and unpinned with a Risks line). ux-and-brand rule 4 (the message says what was wrong and what to pass). data-conventions does not apply.

Tests: could they pass with the bug present? No. The redirect test asserts both the 3xx status and opened == [origin]. The scheme test requires 'unknown url type'. The datetime tests require 'not a datetime'. The clear_cache test seeds a day file so the pre-fix comparison is reached, and asserts the file survives. tests/test_data.py only gains imports and appended tests; no existing test is modified, weakened or deleted. The test lock held from 047eba1 per the build gate record.
Skip markers: the diff adds none (no skip/xfail in the added test lines). The build gate's ratchets details.skip_markers is [], and no plan line declares one.

Claims against today's code (test phase, light pass): the removed line `_OPENER = urllib.request.build_opener(_HTTPSHandler())`, _HTTPSConnection/CONNECT_TIMEOUT/READ_TIMEOUT/MAX_BODY_BYTES, the HTTPError conversion in urllib_fetch, and with_retries returning status < 500 other than 418/429 all hold in app/data/http.py. clear_cache calls parse_date at cache.py:146-147 as the spec says.

Minor observations, not reasons: (a) R10's 'pip install -e . succeeds and git status stays clean' on Linux has been checked only partly, because the sandbox is read-only: a wheel built with the right METADATA and egg-info is ignored. The full install rests on the owner's deploy-gate check, which spec Acceptance allows ('where it can run it'). (b) The verifier noted that a non-editable local build leaves build/, which .gitignore does not cover. That is outside R11's scope.
Drive: not applicable (no commands.drive, no drive files in plan.md).
